item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 111138
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Sun Oct 11 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Post-Tropical
Cyclone Rachel, located inland over southern California and on
Hurricane Simon, located just offshore of southwestern Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
A tropical wave over the far eastern East Pacific is producing
disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Environmental conditions are
expected to be conducive for gradual development, and a tropical
depression is likely to form well south of southern Mexico by the
middle or latter half of the week as the system moves generally
west-northwestward at around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Remnants of Rachel Public Advisory Number 58
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Sun Oct 11 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 111442
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Remnants Of Rachel Advisory Number  58
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 AM MST Sun Oct 11 2026
 
...REMNANTS OF RACHEL BRINGING HEAVY RAINS AND GUSTY WINDS TO
PORTIONS OF THE SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES...
...THIS IS THE LAST NHC ADVISORY ON THIS SYSTEM...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM MST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...35.8N 114.6W
ABOUT 255 MI...415 KM NNE OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNE OR 15 DEGREES AT 29 MPH...46 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The government of Mexico has discontinued all coastal warnings.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.

For more information, Please consult products from your local 
weather office.
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the remnants of Rachel were located near
latitude 35.8 North, longitude 114.6 West. The remnants are moving
toward the north-northeast near 29 mph (46 km/h).
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: High Wind Warnings and Wind Advisories are in effect across 
the southwestern United States. Gusty winds associated with the 
remnants of Rachel are spreading over interior portions of the 
southwestern United States, especially in areas of higher terrain, 
today and tomorrow. For more information, Please consult products 
from your local weather office. 
 
RAINFALL: Rachel and its associated moisture will bring total 
rainfall of 1 to 3 inches, with maximum amounts locally up to 5 
inches from Southern California into the Great Basin and portions of 
the Southwest United States through today. This will continue to 
lead to the potential for significant flash and urban flooding.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with 
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall 
Graphic available at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf and the Flash Flood Risk 
graphic at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ero.
 
SURF: Waves generated by Rachel will continue along the coasts of 
Southern California and northern Baja California today. These waves, 
combined with an incoming long-period southerly swell, will cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Coastal flooding 
and erosion are expected to worsen this morning as the highest waves 
coincide with the high tides and water levels that are already 
running well above predicted levels. Moderate to major coastal 
flooding is expected, with hazardous coastal conditions continuing 
the next few days. Please consult products from your local weather 
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane 
Center on this system. For more information, Please consult 
products from your local weather office at 
https://www.weather.gov/

Rainfall forecasts for the United States can always be found at 
https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/qpf2.shtml 
and outlooks of flash flood risks can be found at 
https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/excessive_rainfall_outlook_ero.php
.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Remnants of Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 58
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Sun Oct 11 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 111444
TCDEP3
 
Remnants Of Rachel Discussion Number  58
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 AM MST Sun Oct 11 2026
 
Satellite images and surface observations indicate that Rachel has 
dissipated over the southwestern United States, and this is the last 
NHC advisory. However, the remnants of Rachel are still producing 
areas of heavy rain and gusty winds over portions of the 
southwestern U.S. The initial intensity is estimated to be around 30 
kt.
 
The remnant trough is forecast to continue to weaken, but the 
associated moisture will likely produce heavy rainfall, flooding, 
and gusty winds across the Southwest U.S. today and tonight.

This is the last tropical cyclone discussion issued by the National 
Hurricane Center on this system. For more information on hazards 
associated with the Remnants of Rachel, Please consult products 
from your local weather office at https://www.weather.gov/

Rainfall forecasts for the United States can always be found at 
https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/qpf2.shtml 
and outlooks of flash flood risks can be found at 
https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/excessive_rainfall_outlook_ero.php

 
Key Messages:
 
1. Damaging wind gusts, especially in areas of higher terrain, are 
forecast to spread farther inland over interior portions of the 
southwestern United States today. High Wind Warnings and Wind 
Advisories are in effect across the southwestern United States.
 
2. Areas of heavy rainfall from the remnants of Rachel and its 
associated moisture will continue to result in the potential for 
significant flash and urban flooding today from Southern California 
into the Great Basin and portions of the Southwest United States.
 
3. Waves generated by Rachel, combined with an incoming long-period
southerly swell, will produce life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions along the coasts of Southern California and northern Baja
California. Major coastal flooding has already been occurring in
some areas, with observed water levels running as much as 1.5 feet
above predictions. Coastal flooding and erosion are expected to
worsen this morning as the highest waves associated with Rachel
coincide with high tides and already elevated water levels.
Hazardous coastal conditions are expected to continue the next few 
days. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 12H  12/0000Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Sun Oct 11 2026 
838 
WTPZ35 KNHC 111452
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Advisory Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
900 AM CST Sun Oct 11 2026
 
...CORE OF EXTREMELY DANGEROUS HURRICANE SIMON NEAR THE COAST OF
WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM CST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.2N 105.3W
ABOUT 65 MI...105 KM WNW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 85 MI...140 KM SSE OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...145 MPH...230 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 345 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...937 MB...27.67 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:

The government of Mexico of discontinued to Tropical Storm Watch
from East of Punta San Telmo to Lazaro Cardenas.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to El Roblito
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM CST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located
near latitude 19.2 North, longitude 105.3 West. Simon is moving
toward the north-northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h) and this general
motion is expected to continue over the next day or two. On the
forecast track, Simon is expected to be very near the coast of
west-central Mexico later today and remain close to the coast on
Monday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 145 mph (230 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Simon is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. While some weakening could occur, Simon is 
still forecast to move very near the coast of west-central Mexico as 
a major hurricane today. More significant weakening could occur if 
the core of Simon moves fully onshore or interacts with the higher 
terrain.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles
(130 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 937 mb (27.67 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are likely beginning in the southern part
of the Hurricane Warning, with hurricane conditions spreading
northward later today into Monday. 
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce additional rainfall totals of 
8 to 16 inches over portions of southwestern Mexico, with isolated 
maximum storm totals of 30 inches possible across portions of 
Michoacan, Colima, and Jalisco through Monday.  This rainfall will 
produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas 
of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge is expected along the immediate 
coast near and to the east of where the center approaches landfall. 
Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and 
destructive waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1200 PM CST.
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Sun Oct 11 2026 
480 
WTPZ45 KNHC 110859
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  16
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
300 AM CST Sun Oct 11 2026

The Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunters provided some valuable 
information on the structure of Simon overnight.  They found 
that the pressure had dropped to 928 mb, with maximum flight-level 
winds of 135 kt within the small inner core.  Similar to the 
afternoon flight, the whole wind field could not be observed. The 
initial intensity is kept at 135 kt for this advisory as a blend of 
the flight-level wind data, assuming a larger undersampling factor 
than normal, with a slight weight on earlier experimental Synthetic 
Aperture Radar (SAR) data, which showed category 5 strength. 

The hurricane has turned north-northwest at about 5 kt.  This 
motion is expected to continue today, bringing the core of the 
hurricane along the coast of southwestern Mexico.  While some of 
the models have shifted more offshore later today, it is simply too 
close to call whether landfall will occur.  Regardless of the exact 
track, dangerous wind, surge, and rainfall effects appear likely 
over portions of west-central Mexico today in the Hurricane Warning 
area.  After today, the model guidance is in poor agreement on what 
happens due to a weak ridge building just north of the cyclone.  
While the new forecast is nudged westward, it is east of the bulk 
of the model guidance, and we are just going to have to wait and 
see how much the high terrain of the Sierra Madre mountains affects 
the hurricane before having any significant forecast confidence.  

Some weakening should start soon due to the hurricane's close 
proximity to land, and recent satellite imagery could be indicative 
of that trend.  However, Simon is still expected to be an extremely 
dangerous hurricane as it passes near southwestern Mexico today.  
The intensity forecast is extremely sensitive to how close Simon 
passes to western Mexico during the next day or so.  With the 
forecast shifting somewhat offshore in a day or two, the weakening 
rate is lowered some from the last advisory.  This is a very low 
confidence forecast because only a small deviation either east or 
west could result in the hurricane rapidly dissipating after 
landfall or keeping more strength offshore.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Catastrophic wind and life-threatening storm surge impacts are
likely along a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a
Hurricane Warning is in effect from Punta San Telmo to El Roblito.
Preparations to protect life and property should be rushed to
completion.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of
southwestern Mexico through this weekend. This rainfall will produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
3. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central
coast of Mexico over the next few days. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 12H  11/1800Z 19.5N 105.4W  125 KT 145 MPH...NEAR COAST
